name: Site configuration: a garage described from APX alone
description: A call-center console onboards Lakeside Garage with nothing but APX: the equipment on each lane with its role, make, model, versions, serial and MAC; what is built into what and which barrier a reader opens; the cameras and where they look; the comms points a call reaches help through; the ids other systems know the garage by; and the change notice that keeps the console's copy current. Part 26 and Part 16.

steps.name: Onboarding day
steps.narration: No spreadsheet from the PARCS vendor, no export from the phone system. The console asks APX.

steps.name: Everything on exit lane 2
steps.narration: Four APDS SupplementalEquipment records, each with the equipment-detail decoration: the barrier, the pay-in-lane terminal that is the exit verifier (it controls the barrier), the intercom built into it, and the overhead camera. The APDS equipment type stays APDS; the role says what each one is. No IP address, no username, no password anywhere (§26.1).

steps.name: Beyond the lanes: the lobby door
steps.narration: Filter by area. The pedestrian entrance has the access door, the card reader that controls it, the intercom in its call box, and a ceiling camera looking at pedestrians. Place-level equipment carries no lane.

steps.name: Every camera in the garage
steps.narration: One role, camera; the camera decoration says where each one is, how it is mounted and what it looks at: the lane, the lobby, the P2 ramp. The ramp camera still speaks RTSP with a password; APX names its vault label, never the password (§26.3 rule 3).

steps.name: Which lane is calling: by the intercom's caller id
steps.narration: A comms point is any way a parker reaches help. The exit-lane intercom calls out as +1 555 010 0201; it resolves to the lane and to the barrier it serves (§26.4).

steps.name: By the posted number a parker dialed
steps.narration: A sign cannot know where the caller stands: the posted number resolves to the place and to no lane. The agent asks.

steps.name: Their id, our record
steps.narration: The PARCS calls the garage LOT-0042. A support tool holding only that asks APX what it is (§26.6).

steps.name: A live look at exit lane 2
steps.narration: A single-use WebRTC link that lives five minutes, bound to the agent and logged against the call.

steps.name: What this garage can do, before a call
steps.narration: Part 16: discovery now says, per place, which commands the site executes and which features it supports. Lakeside has no lostTicket through the API; a console knows that before the first call.

steps.name: Overnight, the exit-lane terminal is swapped
steps.narration: New serial, new MACs, new firmware. The implementation updates the record and subscribers receive apx.equipment.changed.v1; nobody re-reads the garage (§26.7).

steps.name: A console that was offline catches up by change feed
steps.narration: Part 5 §5.2: the same list route, mode=change. Without a cursor it answers with the feed's head; from then on every change arrives whole, and a removal as a tombstone.
